data.title: IntegraGen receives rival takeover bids amid court‑ordered restructuring
data.description:
IntegraGen SA ( (FR:ALINT) ) has provided an update.

IntegraGen SA, a French genomics company focused on cancer and rare genetic diseases, provides advanced DNA sequencing and genomic data interpretation services to academic and private labs. Listed on Euronext Growth Paris, it operates one of France’s largest NGS laboratories and plays a significant role in supporting precision medicine for research institutes and healthcare stakeholders.

IntegraGen announced it has received two takeover offers from Health In Code and ABL Diagnostics as part of a court‑ordered restructuring process initiated in June 2026. The bids, financed with bidders’ own funds, target the company’s activities and assets, but explicitly exclude any purchase of IntegraGen shares.

Key terms of the offers remain confidential and are subject to several conditions precedent, including completion of audits, internal approvals, and assurance that there is no material deterioration of the company’s assets. The Commercial Court of Évry will review and may improve the offers under legal provisions, with a decision on a sale plan expected at a hearing scheduled for October 5, 2026.

Proceeds from any eventual sale would be used to pay creditors, and management warns that the potential resumption of activity may not leave residual value for shareholders, who face a risk of total loss of their investment. A possible delisting of IntegraGen shares from Euronext Growth Paris is also flagged, underscoring the gravity of the restructuring for equity holders.

Despite the ongoing procedure, IntegraGen’s chief executive emphasizes that client and partner activities continue uninterrupted, with teams fully mobilized on ongoing projects. The company views the competing offers as validation of interest in its platform, staff and expertise, and has committed to keep the market informed of material developments as the court‑supervised process advances.

More about IntegraGen SA

IntegraGen SA is a French company specializing in cancer genomics and rare genetic diseases, providing DNA sequencing services and software for interpreting genomic data to academic and private laboratories. It operates one of France’s largest next‑generation sequencing laboratories, serves leading research institutes, and focuses on enabling precision medicine, employing 28 staff and generating €5 million in revenue in 2025.

The company is listed on Euronext Growth Paris and positions itself as a major player in high‑throughput sequencing, targeting the healthcare and research markets with advanced genomic analysis capabilities. Its platform and expert teams form the core of its value proposition to clients seeking sophisticated genomic and data analytics solutions.

IntegraGen’s business model relies on continued demand for cancer and genetic disease diagnostics and research support, with its operations embedded in collaborations with hospitals, research centers, and biotech partners across France and potentially broader European markets. The ongoing restructuring places this positioning under scrutiny as ownership and asset control may change.

data.title: Pharming wins FDA nod to extend Joenja use to younger APDS children
data.description:
Pharming Group ( (NL:PHARM) ) has provided an announcement.

Pharming has secured U.S. FDA approval for new 40 mg and 50 mg twice-daily doses of Joenja (leniolisib) to treat children aged 4 to 11 years who weigh at least 27 kg and have APDS, a rare primary immunodeficiency. This makes Joenja the first FDA-approved therapy for APDS in this younger pediatric group, with the new doses expected to reach patients through Pharming’s specialty distribution network in October.

The expanded indication builds on Joenja’s existing approval for patients 12 and older and is backed by Phase III data showing improvements in key disease markers with a safety profile consistent with earlier use. The move strengthens Pharming’s position in the rare disease space, offers earlier intervention for APDS to potentially prevent irreversible complications, and underscores ongoing efforts to broaden access through additional regulatory filings for lighter pediatric patients.

Pharming Group N.V. is a global biotechnology company headquartered in Leiden, the Netherlands, with operations in the U.S. and Europe. The company develops and commercializes innovative medicines targeting rare immune and genetic diseases, focusing on unmet medical needs in highly specialized patient populations.

Its portfolio includes Joenja (leniolisib), an oral small-molecule PI3Kδ inhibitor that is the first and only approved treatment for activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS) across multiple major markets. data.title: Anvi Global Holdings Approves One-for-Twenty Reverse Split
data.description:
An update from Anvi Global Holdings ( (ANVI) ) is now available.

On September 4, 2026, the majority holder of ANVI Global Holdings, Inc.’s common stock, representing about 60% of the voting capital, executed a written consent approving a one‑for‑twenty reverse stock split of the company’s issued and outstanding shares. The board had recommended this move on August 29, 2026, and under Nevada law the majority stockholder’s consent was sufficient to authorize the action without a physical meeting or vote of minority shareholders.

The reverse stock split is aimed at lifting ANVI’s share price after a June 6, 2026 deficiency notice from OTC Markets Group, which warned that the company’s bid price had stayed below $0.01 for 30 days and threatened its OTCQB listing. Implementation of the split remains contingent on SEC Schedule 14C clearance and FINRA approval, and the company is concurrently requesting a 60‑day extension to meet listing criteria after delays and geopolitical disruptions derailed a planned asset injection strategy to support compliance.
